AGENTS.md — rsmart R Package

Source: AGENTS.md

Project Overview

rsmart is an R package for planning and analyzing Sequential Multiple Assignment Randomized Trials (SMARTs) with normal, binary, and time-to-event endpoints. It implements the IPWE, AIPWE, and IAIPWE estimators from Manschot, Laber, and Davidian (2023), which includes implementation for Wu, Wang, and Wahed (2023) and Zhang, Tsiatis, Laber, and Davidian (2013).

Repository Structure

DESCRIPTION        # Package metadata, dependencies, and versioning
NAMESPACE          # Exported functions (auto-generated by roxygen2)
LICENSE            # Package license
README.md          # Package overview and usage
rsmart.Rproj       # RStudio project file
R/                 # Source code for all package functions
man/               # Documentation files (auto-generated by roxygen2)
data/              # Packaged datasets (.rda files)
data-raw/          # Raw data and scripts to prepare datasets
vignettes/         # Long-form documentation and tutorials
tests/             # Unit tests using the testthat framework

Key Source Files (R/)

  • iaipwe.R — Main entry point: the iaipwe() function implements the IAIPWE estimator for K-stage SMARTs with up to 2 treatment options at each stage.
  • estimate_all_values.R — Estimates values for all treatment regimes.
  • gen_no_trt_resp.R — Generates treatment and response regime lists (gen_no_trt_resp(), regimelist_no_trt_resp()).
  • q_step.R / pi_step.R — Q-learning and propensity score model fitting steps.
  • ee_value.R, ee_value_ipw.R — Estimating equations for value estimation (augmented and IPW).
  • ee_value_derivatives.R, ee_value_derivatives_ipw.R — Derivatives of estimating equations.
  • ee_beta.R, ee_nu.R, ee_pi.R — Estimating equations for model parameters.
  • An.R, Bn.R — Computation of A_n and B_n matrices used in variance estimation.
  • nu.R, kappa.R — Helper functions for nu and kappa terms.
  • value_terms.R — Intermediate value computation terms.
  • get_bounds.R, get_sample_size.R — Confidence bounds and sample size calculations.
  • data.R — roxygen2 documentation for the pcsttrial dataset.

Exported Functions

The package exports many public functions; the list below is a non-exhaustive set of common entry points. Use NAMESPACE as the authoritative source for the complete current public API.

  • iaipwe() — Primary analysis function for IAIPWE estimation.
  • gen_no_trt_resp() — Common helper to generate treatment and response data structures.
  • regimelist_no_trt_resp() — Common helper to generate regime lists for trials without treatment-response interactions.

Data

  • pcsttrial — A simulated dataset (284 observations, 14 variables) mimicking the Pain Coping Skills Training trial. Variables include baseline covariates (pctchange, height, weight, comorbidity, painmed, chemo), stage-2 covariates (pctchangek2, adherence), treatment assignments (a1, a2), a response indicator (r2), and timing variables (study_day_enroll, study_day_rerand, study_day_outcome).

Build & Development

  • Language: R (>= 3.5)
  • Imports (runtime): MASS, Matrix, data.table, doFuture, foreach, modelObj, mvtnorm, stats (see NAMESPACE).
  • Suggests (development/testing): dplyr, knitr, rmarkdown, testthat (>= 3.0.0).
  • Documentation: Generated via roxygen2 (with markdown support). Run devtools::document() to regenerate man/ and NAMESPACE. Never edit man/ or NAMESPACE by hand.
  • Data preparation: Raw data scripts are in data-raw/. Run source("data-raw/pcsttrial.R") to regenerate the packaged dataset in data/.
  • Build & check: Use devtools::build() and devtools::check() (or R CMD build / R CMD check) to build and validate the package. Aim for zero errors, warnings, and notes.
  • Vignettes: Long-form documentation lives in vignettes/. Build with devtools::build_vignettes().
  • Version: The package is in early development (0.0.0.9000).

Coding Conventions

  • Use roxygen2 with markdown for all function documentation.
  • Follow standard R package structure conventions.
  • Internal (non-exported) helper functions do not need the @export tag.
  • Use snake_case for function and variable names.
  • Prefix external package calls with package::function() in code (e.g., dplyr::rename()), or declare imports via @importFrom in roxygen2 headers.

Testing

  • Tests should be added under a tests/testthat/ directory using the testthat framework.
  • Run tests with devtools::test().

Common Tasks

Task Command
Document devtools::document()
Build devtools::build()
Check devtools::check()
Test devtools::test()
Install locally devtools::install()
Build vignettes devtools::build_vignettes()
Regenerate data source("data-raw/pcsttrial.R")

Boundaries

The following guidelines define what AI agents should and should not do when editing this package.

Do

  • Follow existing coding conventions (snake_case, roxygen2 markdown, package::function() prefixing).
  • Add or update roxygen2 documentation when modifying exported functions.
  • Run devtools::document() after changing roxygen2 headers or @importFrom directives.
  • Run devtools::check() after making changes and fix any introduced errors, warnings, or notes.
  • Write or update testthat tests for any new or changed functionality.
  • Keep changes minimal and focused — prefer small, reviewable edits.
  • Preserve the existing package structure and file organization.
  • Update AGENTS.md if structural changes are made (new exported functions, new files, new dependencies).

Do Not

  • Do not edit auto-generated files (man/, NAMESPACE) directly; use devtools::document() instead.
  • Do not change the core statistical methodology (estimating equations, variance formulas, value estimation logic) without explicit instruction. These implement published methods from peer-reviewed papers.
  • Do not add new package dependencies (Imports or Suggests in DESCRIPTION) without explicit approval.
  • Do not modify or delete the pcsttrial dataset or its raw data without explicit instruction.
  • Do not change function signatures of exported functions (argument names, order, or defaults) without explicit instruction, as this is a breaking change.
  • Do not remove existing tests or lower test coverage.
  • Do not commit credentials, patient data, or any sensitive information.
  • Do not change the license or authorship metadata in DESCRIPTION.
